arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Mr. O'Connor argued that officers cannot hold drivers for sniffs without individualized suspicion.
Ms. Anders argued that a reasonableness analysis avoids arbitrary results in traffic stops.
Justice Roberts asked if a dog sniff during a ticket-writing process is permissible.
Justice Scalia questioned whether asking for a license after a warning is allowed.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: This issue defines the boundary between routine traffic enforcement and invasive searches. It determines how long police can detain drivers without probable cause. It shapes the balance between public safety and individual liberty. It impacts millions of daily interactions between citizens and law enforcement.
